question: A shopkeeper sold an article for ₹85.50 at a profit of 12.5%. Had he sold it for ₹81.70, then what would be his profit or loss percentage?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Profit 12.5% = 1/8 → **CP** : **SP₁** = 8 : 9

9 units = ₹85.50 ⇒ 1 unit = ₹9.50

**CP** = 8 × 9.50 = ₹76

New **SP₂** = ₹81.70 ⇒ Profit = 81.70 − 76 = ₹5.70

Profit% = (5.70 / 76) × 100 = 7.5%

**∴ The correct answer is 7.5% profit.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ee5ddd589e98f066e2a40c470c7afe4bde3cfe3ef43f4343ccce2fd9ddd5dc6e.png] 

**Given:**

Selling Price (**SP₁**) = ₹85.50

Profit Percentage (**P₁%**) = 12.5%

New Selling Price (**SP₂**) = ₹81.70

**Formula Used:**

CP = [SP / (100 + P%)] × 100

Profit% = [(SP − CP) / CP] × 100

**Calculations:**

⇒ **Cost Price (CP)** = [85.50 / (100 + 12.5)] × 100

⇒ **CP** = [85.50 / 112.5] × 100

⇒ **CP** = 0.76 × 100 = ₹76

⇒ New Profit = **SP₂** − **CP** = 81.70 − 76 = ₹5.70

⇒ New Profit% = (5.70 / 76) × 100

⇒ New Profit% = 570 / 76 = 7.5%

**∴ The correct answer is 7.5% profit.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Profit and Loss Basics

Profit occurs when **SP > CP**, and Loss occurs when **CP > SP**. Percentage is always calculated on **Cost Price (CP)** unless stated otherwise.

Fractional Conversion

12.5% is equivalent to 1/8. This means for a CP of 8 units, the profit is 1 unit, making the SP 9 units.

Marked Price and Discount

Discount is always calculated on the **Marked Price (MP)**. **SP = MP − Discount**.
